errata.error: UHSLC's station metadata places six series several kilometers from their gauge, one of them in the open sea.
errata.response: The station refresh moves each station to the gauge's position from another source, listed in `POSITIONS` in `src/positions.ts`. An entry applies only while UHSLC still serves the position it was written against; if UHSLC moves the station, it keeps UHSLC's position and the refresh reports the entry and fails the run until a person checks it.
errata.evidence:
| Station | UHSLC | Gauge | Off by | Source of the gauge's position |
| --- | --- | --- | --: | --- |
| Port Stanley 290A, 1964–1974 | -52.7, -57.8667 | -51.690339, -57.864931 | 112 km | PSMSL Stanley (1082), 1964–1974 |
| Port Stanley 290, 1992 on | -51.75, -57.9333 | -51.692358, -57.820514 | 10 km | PSMSL Stanley II (1796), 1992 on |
| Meulaboh 914 | 4.316667, 96.21667 | 4.1274865, 96.131854 | 23 km | IOC sea level monitoring (meul) |
| Acapulco 316 | 16.8417, -99.8517 | 16.8379333, -99.903 | 5.5 km | IOC (acap2); UHSLC's own 316A and 316B, and UNAM's records, are within 1 km of it |
| Kaumalapau 548 | 20.78, -156.9 | 20.79, -156.995 | 10 km | CO-OPS Kaumalapau Harbor (1614465); UHSLC's position is inland on Lanai |
| Chuuk 054A, 1947–1991 | 7.45368, 151.8982 | 7.44667, 151.847 | 5.7 km | NOAA's Moen Island gauge (CO-OPS 1840000); UHSLC's position is its current gauge's |

UHSLC's 290A position sits 112 km south of Stanley in the South Atlantic. slackwater-database tracks the same positions in TICON's copies of these series in [openwatersio/slackwater-database#375](https://github.com/openwatersio/slackwater-database/issues/375).

errata.error: UHSLC's hourly Göteborg-Torshamnen levels are stamped one hour early from 23 July to 31 December 2007.
errata.response: 23 July to 31 December 2007 is flagged `suspect`, keeping UHSLC's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026: the tide's timing at Göteborg ran about 65 minutes early in those windows. Against SMHI's own record of the gauge (`smhi/2109`), UHSLC's values differ by 3.6 to 4.3 cm RMS a month, and by 0.0 cm once shifted 60 minutes; before 23 July and after 31 December they match unshifted. GESLA's copies carry the same values (erratum `gesla-goteborg-2007-hour-early`). GESLA's CMEMS record of the gauge differs from UHSLC's by the same amount over the span, as SMHI's does, so it's on the right clock.

errata.error: UHSLC's hourly Göteborg-Torshamnen levels are stamped one hour early from 1 February to 30 June 2011.
errata.response: February to June 2011 is flagged `suspect`, keeping UHSLC's own flag as `source_flag`.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026: the tide's timing at Göteborg ran about 62 minutes early. Against SMHI's own record (`smhi/2109`) the values differ by 3.5 to 4.8 cm RMS a month, and by 0.0 to 0.2 cm once shifted 60 minutes; January and July onward match unshifted. GESLA's copies carry the same values (erratum `gesla-goteborg-2011-hour-early`). GESLA's CMEMS record of the gauge differs from UHSLC's by the same amount over the span, as SMHI's does, so it's on the right clock.

errata.error: UHSLC's hourly Cuxhaven levels from 29 February to 31 March 2024 don't match the gauge's other records, even allowing for a clock offset.
errata.response: 29 February to 31 March 2024 is flagged `suspect`, keeping UHSLC's own flag as `source_flag`. These are fast-delivery values; check the span again when UHSLC's research-quality release replaces them.
errata.evidence: Found by the cross-station checks in `scripts/cross-check.ts` ([#121](https://github.com/openwatersio/water-levels/pull/121)), November 2026. Against PEGELONLINE's Cuxhaven Steubenhöft (`pegelonline/5990020`) and GESLA's BfG and CMEMS records of the gauge, which agree with each other, UHSLC's March 2024 differs by 56 cm RMS, and still by 38 cm at its best lag of about 45 minutes; April to June and September to December 2024 match to within 0.4 cm. No other gauge in the German Bight matches the month (best r 0.94). GESLA's copy carries it too (erratum `gesla-cuxhaven-uhslc-2024-march`).
